cues.en: All right, our next witness is Dr. Carl Sagan of Cornell University, a man who needs no introduction. He comes to us today from the Center for Radiophysics and Space Sciences. We welcome you, and we're very pleased that you would take the time out of your schedule to come to a place like Washington where everything seems to be living in today and not in tomorrow to share with us your particular view of how our past and our present may well affect our future. Carl, thank you very much.
cues.zh: 接下来，我们的下一位证人是康奈尔大学的卡尔·萨根博士，一位无需介绍的人物。他今天从射电物理学与空间科学中心来到我们这里。我们欢迎您，也非常高兴您能抽出时间，来到华盛顿这样一个似乎一切都活在今天而非明天的地方，与我们分享您对过去和现在如何可能影响未来的独特见解。卡尔，非常感谢。

cues.en: Thanks very much, Senator Dernberger, Senator Gore, Senator Burdick. Glad to be here. As I understand my function, it is to give some sense of what the greenhouse effect is, to try to say something about greenhouse effect on other planets, to again underscore that this is a real phenomenon, and then
cues.zh: 非常感谢，德恩伯格参议员、戈尔参议员、伯迪克参议员。很高兴来到这里。据我理解，我的职责是让大家对温室效应有所了解，谈谈其他行星上的温室效应，再次强调这是一个真实的现象，然后

cues.en: Perhaps I can take liberty to say a few remarks about what to do about it. The power of human beings to affect and control and change the environment is growing as our technology grows. And at present time we clearly have reached the stage where we are capable, both intentionally and inadvertently,
cues.zh: 也许我可以冒昧地就如何应对这一问题说几句。人类影响、控制和改变环境的能力随着技术的进步而不断增强。目前，我们显然已经达到了这样的阶段：我们能够有意或无意地

cues.en: to make significant changes in the global climate and in the global ecosystem. And we've probably been doing, on a smaller scale, things like that for a very long period of time. For example, slash and burn agriculture, which has been with us for tens of thousands of years probably, changes the climate to some extent by changing the albedo, the reflectivity of the Earth.
cues.zh: 对全球气候和全球生态系统做出重大改变。而且很可能在很长一段时间里，我们一直在以较小的规模做这类事情。例如，刀耕火种的农业，可能已经伴随我们数万年之久，它通过改变反照率——即地球的反射率——在一定程度上改变了气候。

cues.en: That massive changes have occurred is clear from the historical record. For example, Egypt was once the breadbasket of the Roman Empire. It may be the same role as the American Midwest plays today. That is certainly no longer the case. It's not a greenhouse effect issue. It may be an overgrazing issue, but is an example of how humans are perfectly capable of making these unexpected and inadvertent.
cues.zh: 历史记录清楚表明，已经发生了巨大的变化。例如，埃及曾是罗马帝国的粮仓，或许扮演着今天美国中西部所扮演的同样角色。但如今肯定已不再如此。这不是温室效应的问题，可能是过度放牧的问题，但这也是人类完全有能力造成这些意外和无心后果的一个例子。

cues.en: changes. Because the effects occupy more than a human generation, there is a tendency to say that they are not our problem. Of course, then there are nobody's problem. Not on my tour of duty, not on my term of office, it's something for the next century, let the next century worry about it. But the problem is that
cues.zh: 变化。由于影响跨越超过一代人的时间，人们往往说这不是我们的问题。当然，那样就成了谁的问题都不是。不在我的任期内，不在我的任期里，那是下个世纪的事，让下个世纪去操心吧。但问题在于，

cues.en: there are effects, and the greenhouse effect is one of them, which have long time constants. If you don't worry about it now, it's too late later on. And so in this issue, as in so many other issues, we are passing on extremely grave problems for our children when the time to solve the problems, if they can be solved at all, is now.
cues.zh: 确实存在一些效应，温室效应就是其中之一，它们具有很长的时间常数。如果你现在不担心，以后就太晚了。因此在这个问题上，正如在许多其他问题上一样，我们正在把极其严重的问题留给我们的孩子，而解决问题的时机——如果还能解决的话——就是现在。

cues.en: If you ask what determines the Earth's climate, clearly the main thing that determines it is sunlight. Sunlight is what heats the Earth. Not all the light that arrives at the Earth from the sun goes to heating the Earth. Some of it is reflected back. It's just the part that is absorbed. And what happens is there's a certain rate at which sunlight is absorbed by the Earth's surface, and there's a certain rate at which the Earth's surface
cues.zh: 如果你问是什么决定了地球的气候，显然主要的决定因素是阳光。阳光是加热地球的来源。并非所有从太阳到达地球的光都用于加热地球，有些被反射回去了，只有被吸收的那部分才起作用。实际情况是，地球表面吸收阳光有一定的速率，而地球表面

cues.en: radiates to space. What comes from the Sun is in the ordinary visible part of the spectrum that our eyes are sensitive to. What the Earth radiates into space is in the infrared part of the spectrum, longer waves than red, that our eyes are not sensitive to, but it's as legitimate a form of light as the kind that we're used to. Now, if you calculate what the temperature of the Earth ought to be,
cues.zh: 向太空辐射也有一定的速率。来自太阳的光处于光谱的普通可见光部分，是我们的眼睛所能感知的。地球向太空辐射的是光谱的红外部分，比红光波长更长，我们的眼睛无法感知，但它和我们习惯的光一样是正当的光的形式。现在，如果你计算地球的温度应该是多少，

cues.en: from how much sunlight is being absorbed, equaling how much infrared radiation would be radiated to space, you find that the Earth's temperature by this simple calculation is too low. It's about 30 centigrade degrees too low. And why is it too low? It's too low because something was left out of the calculation. What was left out of the calculation? The greenhouse effect. The air between us is transparent.
cues.zh: 根据吸收的阳光量等于向太空辐射的红外辐射量，你会发现按这个简单计算，地球的温度太低了，大约低了30摄氏度。为什么太低呢？太低是因为计算中遗漏了某些东西。遗漏了什么？温室效应。我们之间的空气是透明的。

cues.en: except in Los Angeles and places of that sort, in the ordinary visible part of the spectrum. We can see each other. But if our eyes were sensitive at, say, 15 microns in the infrared, we could not see each other. The air would be black between us, and that's because, in this case, carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is very strongly absorbing at 15 microns and other wavelengths in the infrared. Likewise, there are parts of the infrared spectrum where water vapor absorbs, where we could not
cues.zh: 除了洛杉矶这类地方，在光谱中普通可见的范围内。我们能看见彼此。但如果我们的眼睛对红外线中比如15微米波长敏感，我们就看不见彼此了。我们之间的空气会是黑色的，这是因为在这种情况下，二氧化碳。二氧化碳在15微米及其他红外波段吸收非常强烈。同样，红外光谱中有些部分水蒸气会吸收，如果我们只相隔这个房间的距离，我们也会

cues.en: see each other if we were only as far apart as we are in this room. If you add these infrared absorbing gases to a planet, then what happens is the sunlight comes in as before, but when the surface tries to radiate the space in the infrared, it is blocked, it is impeded by the absorbing gases. And so the surface temperature has to rise
cues.zh: 看不见彼此。如果你把这些红外吸收气体加到行星上，那么会发生的是阳光像以前一样照进来，但当表面试图以红外线向太空辐射时，它被阻挡了，被吸收气体阻碍了。因此表面温度必须上升

cues.en: so that there is an equilibrium between what comes in and what goes out. So this is the greenhouse effect. It is a misnomer for more reasons than one. It's a misnomer in particular because that's not how the florist greenhouse works, but that's a very minor point. There are other gases which absorb in the infrared, many of which have been mentioned already, nitrous oxide, methane, the halocarbons, and these are products partly of
cues.zh: 以便输入和输出之间达到平衡。这就是温室效应。这个名字有多重误称。它特别是个误称，因为花店温室并不是这样运作的，但那是很小的一点。还有其他气体在红外吸收，其中许多已经提到过，一氧化二氮、甲烷、卤代烃，这些部分是

cues.en: agriculture, as fertilizers, refrigeration, aerosol spray cans, and so on, all products of our technology. We don't generate much water into the atmosphere, but we certainly do generate a great deal of carbon dioxide through the burning of wood and fossil fuels and apparently benign activity who could object to humans burning oil and coal, gas, and wood.
cues.zh: 农业的产物，作为肥料，制冷、气溶胶喷雾罐等等，都是我们技术的产物。我们不会向大气中产生很多水，但我们确实通过燃烧木材和化石燃料产生了大量二氧化碳，还有看似无害的活动，谁能反对人类燃烧石油、煤炭、天然气和木材呢。

cues.en: I'd like to stress that the greenhouse effect makes life on Earth possible. If there were not a greenhouse effect, the temperature would, as I say, be 30 centigrade degrees or so colder, and that's well below the freezing point of water everywhere on the planet. The oceans would be solid after a while. A little greenhouse effect is a good thing. But there is a delicate balance of these invisible gases, and too much or too little greenhouse effect can mean
cues.zh: 我想强调，温室效应让地球上的生命成为可能。如果没有温室效应，温度会像我说的那样，低大约30摄氏度，远低于地球上各处的冰点。海洋过一段时间就会变成固体。一点温室效应是好事。但这些看不见的气体之间存在微妙的平衡，温室效应过强或过弱都可能意味着

cues.en: too high or too low a temperature. And here we are pouring enormous quantities of CO2 and these other gases into the atmosphere every year with hardly any concern about its long-term and global consequences. Now, certainly not all aspects of how increased CO2 and other gases into the atmosphere affect the climate are known. There are still many uncertainties, although the overall picture is, I think, quite clear.
cues.zh: 温度过高或过低。而我们每年都在向大气中排放大量二氧化碳和其他气体，几乎不关心其长期和全球后果。当然，大气中二氧化碳和其他气体增加如何影响气候，并非所有方面都已知。仍有许多不确定性，尽管我认为总体情况相当清楚。

cues.en: quite widely understood and accepted. But there are questions about aerosols, about clouds. You heat up the Earth. How much increase or decrease in cloudiness is there? How does that change the albedo or reflectivity of the Earth? There's questions about the ocean and its response time to an increase in CO2. There are feedback effects.
cues.zh: 这一点已被广泛理解和接受。但还有关于气溶胶、云层的问题。你让地球升温，云量会增加或减少多少？这又如何改变地球的反照率或反射率？还有关于海洋及其对二氧化碳增加响应时间的问题。还有反馈效应。

cues.en: and therefore it is certainly worthwhile to spend some additional money on further research on the subject. Another point is that the significant temperature changes on the Earth between...
cues.zh: 因此，在这个课题上花一些额外的钱做进一步研究肯定是值得的。另一点是，地球上显著的 temperature 变化在……之间

cues.en: ice ages and out of ice ages, glacial and interglacial time periods, seems to be connected with quite small changes in the amount of sunlight that reaches the Earth due to changes in the Earth's orbital properties, and that is a suggestion that the Earth's climate system may be very delicately dependent on the sorts of factors that we're talking about here, and that's why it makes sense to study past climatic change.
cues.zh: 冰期与间冰期、冰川期与间冰期，似乎与地球轨道变化导致到达地球的太阳光量微小变动有关，这暗示地球气候系统可能极其微妙地依赖于我们在这里讨论的这类因素，因此研究过去的气候变化是有道理的。

cues.en: on the Earth as an attempt to obtain some calibration. Another source of calibration is the other planets. Every planet with an atmosphere has some degree of a greenhouse effect. The most spectacular case by far is the greenhouse effect of Venus. It's the nearest planet, about the same mass, radius, density as the Earth, but it is spectacularly different.
cues.zh: 在地球上试图获得一些校准。另一个校准来源是其他行星。每颗有大气层的行星都有某种程度的温室效应。迄今为止最壮观的是金星的温室效应。它是最近的行星，质量、半径、密度与地球大致相同，但差异惊人。

cues.en: several respects, one of which is that the surface temperature is about 470 degrees centigrade, 900 Fahrenheit, and that enormous temperature is not due to its being closer to the sun because Venus is surrounded with bright clouds, and in fact, because it reflects so much light back to space, if that's all that was happening, it would be cooler, not warmer, than the Earth. The reason for this
cues.zh: 在几个方面，其中之一是表面温度约为470摄氏度，900华氏度，这个巨大的温度并非因为它更靠近太阳，因为金星被明亮的云层包围，事实上，由于它反射大量光线回太空，如果仅此而已，它会比地球更冷，而不是更暖。原因是这个

cues.en: absurdly high temperature on the surface of Venus, which is well understood. I mean, Soviet spacecraft have landed on Venus and, in effect, stuck out a thermometer. There's no doubt that the surface temperature is very high, and later U.S. spacecraft have as well. The reason is a massive greenhouse effect in which carbon dioxide plays the major role. Now, the amount of CO2 in the Venus atmosphere is much larger than here.
cues.zh: 金星表面荒谬的高温，这一点已被充分理解。我的意思是，苏联航天器曾登陆金星，实际上伸出了温度计。毫无疑问表面温度非常高，后来的美国航天器也是如此。原因是巨大的温室效应，其中二氧化碳扮演主要角色。现在，金星大气中的CO2量远大于这里。

cues.en: The atmosphere is almost entirely carbon dioxide and there's 90 times more of it there than here. But it is an indication of what can happen in an extreme case. You look at Mars or Jupiter or Titan, the big moon of Saturn, and you have additional examples of greenhouse effects, different gases, different amounts of sunlight reaching the surface, different planetary albedos and cloudiness.
cues.zh: 大气几乎全是二氧化碳，而且那里的二氧化碳比这里多 90 倍。但这说明了极端情况下可能发生什么。看看火星、木星或土星的大卫星 Titan，你还能看到温室效应的更多例子：不同气体、到达表面的阳光量不同、行星反照率和云量也不同。

cues.en: And in all those cases, there is also a greenhouse effect. In addition, it has been possible to calculate those greenhouse effects fairly accurately, so that the kind of theoretical armamentarium which is used to calculate the greenhouse effect changes on the Earth
cues.zh: 在所有这些情况中，也都存在温室效应。此外，人们已经能够相当准确地计算这些温室效应，因此，用来计算地球温室效应变化的那类理论工具

cues.en: is also used for other planets and therefore can be calibrated to some extent against those other planets. If we keep coming out with the right answer in all those different cases, then probably we understand fairly well how greenhouse effects work. It would, however, be worthwhile along the lines that Senator Gore was talking about to have an increased program through NASA.
cues.zh: 也被用于其他行星，因此可以在一定程度上对照那些行星进行校准。如果我们在所有这些不同情况下都能得出正确结果，那大概就说明我们相当了解温室效应如何运作。不过，按照 Gore 参议员所说的思路，通过 NASA 扩大相关计划是值得的。

cues.en: to understand the greenhouse effects on other planets, this might be a very practical application of planetary exploration. As you've heard, the best estimates, they certainly have some uncertainty attached to them, are that at the present rate of burning of fossil fuels, the present rate of increase of minor infrared-absorbing gases in the Earth's atmosphere, that there will be a several centigrade degree temperature increase
cues.zh: 来理解其他行星上的温室效应；这可能是行星探测的一项非常实际的应用。正如你们所听到的，最佳估计——当然它们都带有一定不确定性——是：按目前的化石燃料燃烧速度，以及地球大气中微量红外吸收气体目前的增加速度，将会出现几摄氏度的升温

cues.en: on the Earth global average by the middle to the end of the next century, and that has a variety of consequences, including redistribution of local climates and through the melting of glaciers, an increase in global sea level. There is concern on a somewhat longer time scale about the collapse of the West Antarctic ice sheet.
cues.zh: 就地球全球平均而言，到下世纪中叶至末叶，这会带来多种后果，包括局地气候重新分布，以及通过冰川融化导致全球海平面上升。在稍长的时间尺度上，人们还担心西南极冰盖崩塌。

cues.en: and a general rise of many, many meters in sea level. So we have a kind of handwriting on the wall. Certainly there's more research to be done, but as I say, there is a consensus, what can be done about it? The idea that we should immediately stop burning fossil fuel has such severe economic consequences that no one, of course, will take it seriously. But there are
cues.zh: 以及海平面普遍上升许多许多米。所以我们看到了一种不祥的征兆。当然，还有更多研究要做，但正如我所说，已经存在共识，那对此能做些什么呢？认为我们应当立即停止燃烧化石燃料的想法会带来如此严重的经济后果，以至于当然没有人会认真对待它。但是还有

cues.en: many other things that can be done. One has to do with subsidies for fossil fuels. More efficient use could be encouraged by fewer government subsidies. Secondly, there are alternative energy sources, some of which are useful, at least locally. Solar power is certainly one that might be of more general use. Safe
cues.zh: 许多其他事情可以做。其中之一与化石燃料补贴有关。通过减少政府补贴，可以鼓励更高效的使用。其次，还有替代能源，其中一些是有用的，至少在当地如此。太阳能无疑是可能得到更普遍使用的一种。安全的

cues.en: fission power plants, which are, in principle, possible, and then, on a longer time scale, the prospect of fusion power. Fission and fusion power plants, in principle, vent no infrared active gases and, therefore, whatever other problems they may provide, they do not provide a greenhouse problem.
cues.zh: 裂变发电厂，原则上这是可能的，然后在更长的时间尺度上，还有聚变发电的前景。裂变和聚变发电厂原则上不排放红外活性气体，因此，无论它们可能带来其他什么问题，它们都不会带来温室问题。

cues.en: I'd like to close by just saying a few words on the kind of perspective that this problem, as related problems, pose to us. Here is a problem which transcends our particular generation. It is an intergenerational problem. If we don't do the right thing now, there are very serious problems that our children and grandchildren will have to face.
cues.zh: 最后，我想就这个问题以及相关问题向我们呈现的视角说几句。这是一个超越我们这一代人的问题。这是一个代际问题。如果我们现在不做正确的事，我们的子孙后代将不得不面对非常严重的问题。

cues.en: It is also a global problem. It is no good if just one or two major industrial nations take major steps to prevent a major increase further in CO2 and other greenhouse gases because other nations may, through their industrial development, cause the problem by themselves. And not to say that this is inevitable, but just to give an example.
cues.zh: 这也是一个全球性问题。如果只有一两个主要工业国家采取重大措施来防止二氧化碳和其他温室气体进一步大幅增加，那是没有用的，因为其他国家可能会通过它们的工业发展，自己造成这个问题。并不是说这是不可避免的，只是举个例子。

cues.en: The largest coal reserves on the planet are the United States, Soviet Union and China. China is undergoing a very major industrial development and the burning of coal is certainly something that must be very attractive for the Chinese looking into the future. I would say that there is no way to solve this problem even if the United States and the Soviet Union.
cues.zh: 地球上最大的煤炭储量在美国、苏联和中国。中国正在进行非常重大的工业发展，而燃烧煤炭对展望未来的中国人来说，肯定是非常有吸引力的。我想说，即使美国和苏联……

cues.en: were to come to a perfectly good accord on this issue without involving China and many other nations that will be developing rapidly in the time period we're talking about. So here is a sense in which the nations to deal with this problem have to make a change from their traditional concern
cues.zh: 在这个问题上达成完美良好的协议，如果不把中国和其他许多在我们所谈论的时期内将快速发展的国家包括进来，这个问题也无法解决。所以从某种意义上说，处理这个问题的国家必须改变它们传统的关注点——

cues.en: about themselves and not about the planet and the species. A change from the traditional short-term objectives to longer-term objectives. And we have to bear in mind that in problems like this, the initial stages of global temperature increase, one region of the planet might benefit while another region of the planet suffers. And there has to be a kind of trading off of benefits and...
cues.zh: 只关心自己，而不关心地球和物种。从传统的短期目标转变为长期目标。我们必须记住，在这类问题中，在全球气温上升的初期阶段，地球上的一个地区可能受益，而另一个地区则遭受损失。而且必须有一种利益权衡……

cues.en: suffering and that requires a degree of international amity which certainly doesn't exist today. I think that what is essential for this problem is a global consciousness, a view that transcends our exclusive identifications with the generational and political groupings into which by accident we have been born. The solution to these problems requires a perspective that embraces the planet and the future
cues.zh: 我们正承受着苦难，而这需要一定程度的国际友好氛围，显然今天并不存在。我认为，这个问题的关键在于一种全球意识，一种超越我们偶然生于其中的世代和政治集团狭隘认同的视野。解决这些问题需要一种放眼整个星球和未来的视角

cues.en: because we are all in this greenhouse together. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
cues.zh: 因为我们同处这一个温室之中。谢谢您，主席先生。
